Trafigura Group Pte Ltd Announces Major Investment to Expand Singapore Oil Storage Capacity

Singapore-based commodities trading giant Trafigura Group Pte Ltd has unveiled plans to invest approximately US$400 million in expanding its oil storage and blending infrastructure on Jurong Island, marking a significant step in strengthening its strategic presence in Asia’s energy markets.

According to a company statement released on Tuesday, the investment will support the construction of new storage tanks, blending facilities, and associated logistics infrastructure, increasing total capacity by 30% to 4.2 million cubic meters over the next two years. The expansion is expected to begin in the third quarter of this year and will create around 200 jobs during peak construction, with 40 new permanent roles added upon completion.

“This investment reflects our commitment to Singapore as a vital hub in the global energy supply chain,” said Jean-Luc Maret, Trafigura’s Head of Asia-Pacific Operations. “By enhancing our storage and blending capabilities, we are better positioned to serve regional demand and respond to evolving market dynamics.”

Singapore remains the world’s largest bunkering port and a key transshipment center for crude oil and refined products, handling nearly 1.4 billion tonnes annually. Analysts suggest that Trafigura’s expansion aligns with rising demand for refined fuels and the growing importance of Asia in global commodity flows.

“Expanding infrastructure on Jurong Island reinforces Singapore’s status as a premier oil trading and logistics center,” said Dr. Felicia Tan, senior analyst at the Singapore Energy Institute. “It will also help companies like Trafigura respond to changes in product specifications and tighter environmental regulations in the shipping sector.”

The investment comes amid steady recovery in oil demand across the region and ongoing shifts in trade patterns. Trafigura’s new facilities will be equipped with advanced automation and emissions-reduction technologies, in line with Singapore’s Green Plan 2030.

The Singapore Oil & Gas Producers Association welcomed the announcement, describing the project as “a timely boost to the sector’s competitiveness and innovation.” The group added that the expansion would generate positive spillover effects for supporting industries, including engineering, shipping, and utilities.

Trafigura Group Pte Ltd expects the expanded site to be fully operational by mid-2026, reinforcing the company’s long-term commitment to Singapore and the wider Asia-Pacific region.
